title: Curcumin Alleviates Bone Cancer Pain by Inhibiting Satellite Glial Cell Activity via Janus Kinase 1/Signal Transducer and Transcription 3 Pathway Activator.
authors: Jiang, Xinchao; Song, Yi; Fang, Mei; Wang, Xin; Zhang, Biao; Li, Haiyong; Qian, Jianxue
one_liner_zh: 该文研究姜黄素通过JAK1/STAT3通路缓解骨癌痛，虽用分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Curcumin is the main active component of Curcuma longa L and has anti-inflammatory, antitumor, and neuroprotective properties, making it a potential candidate for bone cancer pain management. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to screen and validate core therapeutic targets of curcumin in bone cancer pain. An in vivo mouse model of bone cancer pain was established via intrafemoral injection of Lewis lung cancer cells. A series of in vivo assays was conducted to evaluate pain sensitivity, bone microstructure, inflammatory cytokines, pain-related neuropeptides, and protein expression levels. In silico analysis verified that curcumin has a strong binding affinity for JAK1 and STAT3. In vivo results demonstrated that curcumin dose-dependently elevated the paw withdrawal threshold and latency, as well as ameliorated bone mineral density and bone destruction. Curcumin also suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines, substance P, calcitonin gene-related peptides, and inhibited satellite glial cell activation by blocking the JAK1/STAT3 pathway. Notably, JAK1 agonist (RO8191) co-administration markedly reversed the analgesic effects of curcumin. Curcumin targets the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway, inhibits satellite glial cell activation, downregulates pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and pain-related neuropeptide expression. Therefore, curcumin exerted a significant analgesic effect against bone cancer pain. Elucidating the analgesic mechanism revealed the core therapeutic targets of curcumin in treating bone cancer pain. This study provides experimental evidence for further research on bone cancer pain.
abstract_zh: 姜黄素是姜黄（Curcuma longa L.）的主要活性成分，具有抗炎、抗肿瘤和神经保护特性，使其成为骨癌痛管理的潜在候选药物。通过网络药理学、分子对接和分子动力学模拟，筛选并验证了姜黄素在骨癌痛中的核心治疗靶点。通过股骨内注射Lewis肺癌细胞建立了骨癌痛的小鼠体内模型。进行了一系列体内实验，以评估疼痛敏感性、骨微结构、炎症细胞因子、疼痛相关神经肽及蛋白表达水平。计算机模拟分析证实，姜黄素对JAK1和STAT3具有强结合亲和力。体内结果表明，姜黄素剂量依赖性地提高了缩爪阈值和潜伏期，并改善了骨矿物质密度和骨破坏情况。姜黄素还抑制了促炎细胞因子、P物质、降钙素基因相关肽，并通过阻断JAK1/STAT3通路抑制了卫星胶质细胞活化。值得注意的是，与JAK1激动剂（RO8191）联合给药显著逆转了姜黄素的镇痛效果。姜黄素靶向JAK1/STAT3信号通路，抑制卫星胶质细胞活化，下调促炎细胞因子释放及疼痛相关神经肽表达。因此，姜黄素对骨癌痛表现出显著的镇痛作用。阐明镇痛机制揭示了姜黄素治疗骨癌痛的核心治疗靶点。本研究为骨癌痛的进一步研究提供了实验证据。
